name: EOMONTH
description: EOMONTH returns the last day of the month that is a given number of months before or after a start date, useful for month-end reporting and period boundaries.
tldr: Returns the last day of the month offset by n months.

parameters.name: months
parameters.description: The number of months to move. Positive moves forward, negative moves backward. The value is truncated to an integer.

basicExample.description: Last day of the same month
basicExample.explanation: Zero months offset returns the end of January 2024, which is Jan 31 (serial 45321).

advancedExamples.title: Last day of the next month in a leap year
advancedExamples.description: One month forward lands on Feb 29 in 2024
advancedExamples.explanation: 2024 is a leap year, so the last day of February is the 29th (serial 45350).

advancedExamples.title: Last day of the previous month
advancedExamples.description: A negative months value goes backward
advancedExamples.explanation: One month before is December 2023, whose last day is Dec 31 (serial 45290).

howItWorks: EOMONTH first moves start_date by the supplied number of months, then returns the serial number of the final day of that resulting month. It is often combined with DATE to build the first day of a month (e.g. EOMONTH(...)-DAY(...)+1).

howToSteps.name: Enter the start date
howToSteps.text: Provide a date serial or DATE(...) expression.

howToSteps.name: Enter the month offset
howToSteps.text: Use a positive or negative integer for months.

howToSteps.name: Format as a date
howToSteps.text: The result is a serial; apply a date format to view it.

limitations: The months argument is truncated to an integer (1.9 becomes 1).
Negative months go backward in time.
The result is a serial number and needs a date format to be readable.

commonErrors.cause: The start_date is not a valid date serial.
commonErrors.fix: Pass a real date value or DATE(...) expression.
Remember positive months move forward, negative move backward.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: EOMONTH works identically in Google Sheets with the same arguments.

faq.question: How do I get the first day of the month?
faq.answer: Use EOMONTH(date,-1)+1 for the prior month-end plus one, or DATE(YEAR(date),MONTH(date),1).

faq.question: What does a 0 month offset return?
faq.answer: The last day of the same month as start_date.

faq.question: Is the leap day handled automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, EOMONTH returns Feb 29 in leap years and Feb 28 otherwise.
